text_a: Processors that want to distribute VisaNet Settlement Service (VSS) reports directly to clients can have the acquiring or issuing identifier identified in their report records. When this option is selected, the acquiring or issuing identifier of the lowest-level SRE is placed in the Destination Identifier field of the machine-readable (TC 46) and print-ready (TC 47) report records. This destination identifier identifies the report records of the client that owns the acquiring or issuing identifier. Reports are grouped under the acquiring or issuing identifier. The Edit Package strips the header information from reports, which includes the Destination Identifier field on print-ready (TC 47) records. Processors that choose the Destination Identifier field to facilitate report distribution must pull the TC 47 records from the original delivery file (ITF). If the acquiring or issuing identifier identification option is not used, the processor identifier is placed in the Destination Identifier field. The processor is always in the report records for summary-level SREs.

The acquiring or issuing identifier identification option can be used to affect the sequence that report records are received. If the acquiring or issuing identifier is identified in report records, the records are received in acquiring or issuing identifier sequence.

text_a: The entity used by the clearing systems to determine processing rules. In

BASE II clearing, a clearing entity is a 6-digit, Visa-assigned acquiring or issuing identifier or an ISO-assigned card range. In the Single Message System (SMS), a clearing entity is the 6-digit, Visa-assigned acquiring or issuing identifier contained in the affiliate ID. The clearing entity is always included in the definition of a lowest-level settlement reporting entity (SRE).
